editorial: This report contains trends that have emerged for the first time today, without repeating records included in normal reports from the last 30 days.

items.title: bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
items.summary: Gods-eye-view is a spatial intelligence simulator that visualizes real-time satellite data on a browser-based 3D globe. Developed with JavaScript, this open-source project allows users to examine live data on Earth through a photorealistic interface.

items.title: abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus
items.summary: GitNexus is a code analysis engine that runs in the browser and transforms code repositories into an interactive knowledge graph. Using local or cloud-based Git repositories, it offers a built-in Graph RAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation) agent to make sense of the codebase.

items.title: abi/screenshot-to-code
items.summary: Screenshot-to-code is a software tool that analyzes screenshot files and converts them into clean HTML, Tailwind, React, or Vue code. It allows developers to quickly turn interface designs into working code snippets.

items.title: NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra
items.summary: Ghidra, developed by the National Security Agency (NSA), is a comprehensive analysis framework used for software reverse engineering processes. Written in Java, this tool allows security researchers to perform detailed examinations by deciphering the code structure of binary files.

items.title: tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
items.summary: FreeLLMAPI combines 34 different free large language model providers into a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. With intelligent routing and automatic error handling features, it allows developers to test different models through a single interface.

items.title: Saving 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1's DNS cache
items.summary: Cloudflare saved 100 terabytes in memory usage by optimizing its 1.1.1.1 Domain Name System (DNS) cache. This improvement aims to reduce server costs by increasing efficiency in data structures.

items.title: "IT WoRKs BeTter in the App "
items.summary: The common belief that mobile applications offer better performance and user experience compared to websites is being questioned through technical constraints and developer preferences. Despite the development of web standards, the fact that some services offer app-specific features to steer users toward native software creates debates over the open nature of the internet.

items.title: Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was unlawful, US judge rules
items.summary: A US court found the blacklisting of AI company Anthropic by the Pentagon to be unlawful. This decision redefines the legal boundaries of restrictions on the use of generative AI in defense industry projects.

items.title: Doctors are finally learning to manage antidepressant withdrawal
items.summary: The medical world is reviewing treatment protocols following increasing complaints from patients experiencing antidepressant withdrawal syndrome. Experts are working on new approaches that involve reducing medication dosages more slowly and in a controlled manner.

items.title: Luanti removed from Google Play due to baseless AI copyright notice
items.summary: The open-source game engine Luanti has been removed from the Google Play store due to an artificial intelligence-based false copyright infringement notice. This situation opens up a discussion on the negative impacts of automated content moderation systems on developers and the responsibilities of platforms in this process.

items.title: zai-org/GLM-5.3
items.summary: GLM-5.3, developed by Zai, is an artificial intelligence model optimized for text generation tasks. Shared on Hugging Face, this model is used in text creation processes within the large language models category.

items.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
items.summary: TacForcing is a method that updates motion plans by processing tactile feedback in real-time during robotic manipulation processes. Unlike existing vision-language-action models, it eliminates the need for complex controllers by enabling the system to react according to physical contact conditions that change during action.

items.title: What Does an Evaluation License? A Commit-Bound Census of Claim-Relative Inference in Inspect Evals
items.summary: This study, shared by Hugging Face, examines the verifiability of metrics in evaluation tools (Inspect Evals) that measure the performance of artificial intelligence models. The research reveals that the data and methods used in current testing processes lack the transparency required to reproduce the claimed results.

items.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming
items.summary: EditaLive offers a framework that makes human-centric video editing processes real-time in live broadcasts. Unlike existing editing tools, the method maintains facial expression consistency and eliminates the requirement for offline processing.

items.title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: PILOT in the Loop allows artificial intelligence agents to improve their performance by using the experiences they gain during long-term tasks in real-time. Unlike traditional models, this method allows agents to correct their errors by applying learned information during the ongoing work process rather than after the task is finished.

items.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models
items.summary: Instead of traditional video data used to train world models, it is proposed to use verifiable data trajectories created in game development environments. It is argued that, similar to AI agents that write code, executable game environments provide high-quality reward signals for reinforcement learning.

items.title: EasyEffects should be part of every Linux distribution to improve laptop speaker sound quality
items.summary: EasyEffects is an audio effects tool that processes audio signals and improves speaker quality on Linux systems. It is suggested that this software be included as a standard in all Linux distributions to balance low hardware performance on laptops.

items.title: OpenOffice does not print on Tuesdays (2009)
items.summary: A printing error encountered in a specific version of the open-source office software OpenOffice was caused by a logic bug that resulted in the software not working only on Tuesdays. This situation demonstrates that bugs in complex codebases can emerge due to conditions that appear unexpected and coincidental.

items.title: Quest for eternal dock on Wayland - lambdock (C + GTK4 + Lisp GNU Guile Scheme)
items.summary: Lambdock is an open-source tool that aims to provide a persistent application launcher on the Wayland display server. Developed using C, the GTK4 interface library, and the GNU Guile Scheme programming language, this project provides a customizable taskbar experience in desktop environments.

A method used by artificial intelligence to reach more accurate information by using the relationships between interconnected data while generating answers.
